meta.title: Vimdow — Vim-style window management for macOS
meta.description: Move, resize, snap, and switch macOS windows from the keyboard with Vim's hjkl, counts, and undo. Free and open source.

hero.lead: Vimdow is a keyboard-driven window manager for macOS. Press one shortcut to enter command mode, then move, resize, snap, and switch windows with h, j, k, l, counts, and undo. The mouse stays where it is.

demo.aria: Animated demo: in command mode a window is moved, widened, centered, snapped to the left half, and restored with Vim keys.
demo.videoUnsupported: Your browser cannot play this video.

steps.right: l moves the window right, one step per press.
steps.grow: Option–l widens it, keeping the top-left corner in place.
steps.center: zz centers it on the display.
steps.half: Control–W, then H fills the left half.

why.title: Why Vimdow
why.p1: Vimdow was written by someone who has used Vim since 1998 and would rather not reach for the mouse. Most of a Mac can be driven from the keyboard, but window management could not: nudging a window a few points, or moving it to another display, always meant leaving the home row.
why.p2: The first version, in 2013, was a small Objective-C app that fixed exactly that for one user. Instead of new shortcuts to learn, it mapped window operations onto the Vim vocabulary: hjkl to move, a count to repeat, 0 and $ for the edges, gg and G for top and bottom, zz to center, u to undo, / to search. In 2026 it was rewritten in Swift 6 with a tested command engine.
why.p3: Vimdow is modal, like Vim. It is not a tiling window manager and does not arrange windows for you; it makes arranging them yourself fast. It is one person's preference, shared for anyone whose hands have the same habits.

enter.title: Enter command mode
enter.text_html: Press <kbd>⌃</kbd><kbd>⌥</kbd><kbd>A</kbd> and release. Until you leave, keys go to Vimdow instead of the frontmost app.

move.title: Move and resize
move.text_html: <kbd>h</kbd> <kbd>j</kbd> <kbd>k</kbd> <kbd>l</kbd> move the focused window by a configurable step. Type a count to repeat, hold a key to glide, add Option or Shift to resize.

leave.title: Leave
leave.text_html: Press <kbd>esc</kbd> or <kbd>.</kbd> to return to normal mode. Your typing goes back to the app.

move.title: Move and resize with counts
move.text: Steps are configurable, keys repeat while held, and every change glides into place. 12j moves twelve steps; Option and Shift resize from opposite corners.

snap.title: Snap and tile
snap.text: 0, $, gg, G, and zz put a window at an edge or the center, keeping its size. Control–W with H, J, K, L, or O fills a half or the whole display.

undo.title: Undo and redo, per window
undo.text: u and Control–R step through each window's own history of moves, resizes, snaps, and display changes, even after you dragged it by hand.

displays.title: Displays that remember
displays.text: Control–Option–K and L send a window to the next display. Coming back restores the frame it had there.

switch.title: Switch without hunting
switch.text: Q shows up to nine numbered windows; type a digit to focus one. / searches by application name, and n and N cycle through the matches.

settings.title: Yours to tune
settings.text: Set separate move and resize steps, choose whether resizing stops at display edges, turn the glide off, and rebind the five global shortcuts.

cheat.title: Command mode at a glance
cheat.intro: Enter with Control–Option–A (the default). Digits typed before a command repeat it. Two keys shown together are pressed one after the other.
cheat.note: Keys are bound to physical ANSI positions, so they stay in the same place on JIS, Korean, and other layouts.

rows.move: Move left, down, up, right by one step
rows.resizeTL: Resize, keeping the top-left corner fixed
rows.resizeBR: Resize, keeping the bottom-right corner fixed
rows.undo: Undo / redo the focused window's last change
rows.edges: Move to the left / right edge of the display
rows.topBottom: Move to the top / bottom edge
rows.halves: Fill the left / bottom / top / right half
rows.numbered: Focus a numbered window; Q again shows the next nine
rows.search: Search by application name; next / previous match

get.title: Get Vimdow
get.intro: For macOS 14 or later, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. The app is signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple.
get.move: Move Vimdow.app from the downloaded zip to Applications.
get.allow: Open it, then allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility.
get.accessibilityText: macOS requires it for any app that moves another app's windows. Vimdow uses it for that and nothing else: no network access, no analytics, nothing leaves your Mac.

footer.credits: Jang Ho Hwang has been building Vimdow since 2013. Yoo Yong-Ha wrote its first command window the same year. Global shortcuts use the KeyboardShortcuts library (MIT License).
footer.privacy: This site sets no cookies and runs no analytics.
